SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams presents a genuinely mixed picture that lands near neutral. The franchise is high-quality — #1 global coatings company, ~4,900 company-operated stores creating structural contractor lock-in, ~49% gross margins, and ROE still near 59%. Q1 2026 beat consensus on both revenue ($5.67B, +6.8% YoY) and adjusted EPS ($2.35 vs $2.27 consensus), and management reiterated full-year guidance of $11.50–$11.90 EPS. However, the fundamental trajectory is deteriorating: Q1 standalone operating margin compressed to ~12% (vs mid-teens in prior quarters), operating cash flow collapsed to $139.1M (−89% QoQ from Q3 2025), and net margin has narrowed from 11.6% to 10.9%. The balance sheet carries 2.1x debt-to-equity from the Valspar legacy. Valuation is cheap relative to SHW's own history — P/E of 28.6x and P/B of 16.8x are both at the floor of their 365-day ranges — but the earnings yield of 3.5% sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47%, meaning the 'cheapness' is partly justified by margin compression and a pushed-out housing recovery timeline (UBS expects no above-average growth until 2028+). Elevated oil at $96.83/bbl adds raw-material cost headwind. The UBS downgrade to Neutral (June 2, 2026, PT cut to $330 from $385) reflects the balanced risk/reward. No clear near-term fundamental catalyst exists to re-rate the stock. The score reflects a durable franchise offset by real earnings deterioration and no catalyst — essentially a hold.
key_factors: Q1 2026 revenue $5.67B, +6.8% YoY; adjusted EPS $2.35 beat $2.27 consensus — business still growing
Q1 standalone operating margin ~12% vs mid-teens in Q2/Q3 2025 — margin compression is the central concern
Operating cash flow $139.1M in Q1, down 89.4% QoQ from Q3 2025's $1.31B — cash conversion deteriorated sharply
P/E 28.6x and P/B 16.8x at floor of 365-day ranges (28.0–37.1x and 16.4–22.1x respectively) — cheap vs own history
Earnings yield 3.5% below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47% — not cheap on absolute/risk-adjusted basis
Debt-to-equity 2.1x ($9.32B debt, $4.43B equity) — elevated leverage from Valspar acquisition
Gross margin stable at ~49% — franchise pricing power intact; ROE still 58.7% though declining from 64.9%
Full-year 2026 guidance reiterated: adjusted EPS $11.50–$11.90, low-to-mid single-digit sales growth
UBS downgraded to Neutral June 2, 2026; PT cut to $330; no above-average growth expected until 2028+
WTI oil at $96.83/bbl — elevated petrochemical input costs contributing to margin headwind
~4,900 company-operated stores with 50–55% contractor revenue mix — structural competitive moat intact
No clear near-term fundamental catalyst to drive re-rating; housing recovery timeline pushed to 2028+
